sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident caused on 23.11.2021.

The brief facts are as under: It is submitted that on 23.11.2021 at about 05.40 p.m when the petitioner was going towards Market from his employer hardware shop by riding a Honda Activa bearing No.KA02JS7645, when he reached near Y.Ramachandra Road at Vijaya Cafe Hotel towards Kanakadasa Junction side, at that time one Maruthi Swift Car bearing No.KA02MQ 9634 came from same direction i.e., from Gubbi Rangamandira, Opp.Majestic Mall, Gandhinagar,
6th main towards Darga side with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, lost control over his vehicle, went to wrong side and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle from behind.
Due to this the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Srinivasa hospital, Bengaluru, wherein Xrays were taken and fractures were noticed and advised for surgery and then shifted to Chord Road hospital, Bengaluru and admitted as inpatient and has undergone surgery.
The petitioner had spent Rs.5,39,786/ towards treatment and other incidental charges.

That the petitioner prior to accident was hale and healthy and was working as part time worker in Hardware shop and also studying (SCCH3) 4 M.V.C.No.461/2022 3rd year BBA course and earning Rs.23,000/ p.m.
Due to the accident he has become disabled to continue his work and study.
Now the petitioner is getting giddiness and he is able to study properly and lost his future.
Even the marriage prospectus of the petitioner was greatly diminished.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of car driver.
Even a criminal case is registered against the said car driver.
The respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said Car are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence this petition.
03. After service of notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before this court on the date fixed for his appearance and hence he was placed absent through out the proceedings of the petition.

However the respondent No.2 have appeared before this Court through their counsel and filed written statement.
04.
The averments of the written statement of the respondent No.2 is as under: It is false that the petitioner has sustained injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of car driver.

This respondent Sri.H.P.Revanth vs Sri.Siddesh.D.R on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70548591/
2 is the insurer of Car bearing No.KA02MQ9634, but liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
The car driver has no (SCCH3) 5 M.V.C.No.461/2022 valid driving licence on the date of accident.
The accident does not took place due to the negligence of offending car driver, but due to the petitioner himself.
This respondent denies manner of accident, age, avocation and income of the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner.
The claim of the petitioner is exorbitant and prays to dismiss the petition.
05. In order to prove the case, the petitioner and doctor were got examined as PW.1 and 2 and got marked 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to 17 and closed his side.
06. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.2 submit no oral evidence.

07. Heard both sides.
08.
Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed:

ISSUES 01.Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 23.11.2021 at about 05.40 p.m, near Y.Ramachandra Road, in front of Gubbi Veeranna Rangamandira, opposite to Majestic Mall, Gandhinagar, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent act of the driving of the Car bearing registration No. KA02MQ9634 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
(SCCH3) 6 M.V.C.No.461/2022 02.Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03
. What Order or Award?
09. My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under: Issue No.1 In affirmative Issue No.2 In partly affirmative Issue No.3
As per final order for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is the grievance of the petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of car driver.
Due to the accident he had sustained disability and put into hardship.

The same was opposed by the respondent No.2 and contended that the accident did not took place due to the negligence of car driver and it is due to the negligence of petitioner himself,
hence they are liable to pay compensation.
In order to prove this, the petitioner himself got examined as PW.1 by reiterating all the averments of the petition in his affidavit.
The PW.1 in his cross examination has admitted that "It is true that at the time of accident I had completed IV semester.

It is true that now I had completed all Sri.H.P.Revanth vs Sri.Siddesh.D.R on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70548591/
3 semester and BBA.
That the motorcycle ridden by me on the date of accident belongs to my owner Champalal.
That I had lodged complaint to the police at Srinivasa hospital.
It is true that in this accident both vehicles are damaged.
It is true that the accident took place at junction.
It is true that as per the police records at the time of accident I was student".
The PW.1 had denied other suggestion of the respondent No.2 counsel.
12. The PW.1 in support of the case had got marked entire police records as per Ex.P.1 to 7.
On perusal of these documents, it is clear that the concerned I.O after investigation has filed Charge sheet against offending Car driver for the alleged offences punishable U/s 279, 338 of IPC.
Further after investigation the I.O contended that the petitioner sustained injuries due to rash and negligent driving of Car driver only.

Eventhough the respondent No.2 contend that the accident occurred due to the negligence of petitioner only, but in their support they have not adduced any supportive oral and documentary evidence.
14.
The petitioner has produced mahazar and sketch as per Ex.P.3 and 4.

It is true that as per Ex.P.4 the accident took place on Y.Ramachandra Road, near Gubbi Veerannna Rangamandira,
Gandhinagar, Bengaluru.
The Ex.P.5 IMV report shows the damages sustained by offending Car to its front right side.
It is also true that the motorcycle ridden by the petitioner on the date of accident was also got damaged.
But this does not mean that the petitioner was negligent for the accident.

Hence with the available documents on record and in absence of rebuttal evidence by respondent No.2, I am of opinion that the petitioner has proved that he had sustained injuries only due to the rash and negligent driving of offending Car driver.
Hence, I answered issue No.1 in affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:
Further the petitioner has stated that due to the accident he is not able to do (SCCH3) 9 M.V.C.No.461/2022 work as earlier and sustained disability.
In this regard the petitioner has got examined Orthopedic Surgeon as PW.2 who had stated that petitioner had sustained left fracture both bone forearm and he had undergone surgery.

That on examination he found the petitioner has mild swelling of left forearm, plain and tenderness over the fracture site and wrist joint, range of movements of left elbow, wrist restricted, daily activities which requires over head abduction, lifting weight were found to be difficult.

The Xray shows fracture union with implant in situ.
16.
The PW.2 had assessed permanent physical disability to the upper limb is 47% and to whole body at 16%.

The PW.2 has got marked Outpatient record and Xray as per Ex.P.16 and 17.
17.
The PW.2 in his cross examination has admitted that "I have not obtained opinion from the treated doctor It is true that I had assessed only physical disability.
It is true that the fractures are united.
It is true that the movement of shoulder is normal.
It is true that the petitioner has sustained injuries to his left hand.
That the fracture is on middle 1/3rd of left forearm.
It is true that the petitioner right (SCCH3) 10 M.V.C.No.461/2022 hand dominant person.

It is true that there is no Sri.H.P.Revanth vs Sri.Siddesh.D.R on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70548591/
4 amputation".
18.
Hence, from the oral evidence of PW.2 and Ex.P.16 and 17 it is true that the petitioner has sustained disability due to the accident, but not as stated by the PW.2.
Even looking into the age of the injured, nature of treatment obtained and the medical records, I just feel it proper to consider 12% disability for the petitioner.

19. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following heads:
a). Loss of future income:
The PW.1 has stated that he was working as part time worker in Hardware shop and also studying 3rd year BBA course and earning Rs.23,000/ p.m.
In this regard he had produced identity card issued by Geetha Educational Trust and Marks sheet of II and IV semester of Bangalore University as per Ex.P.13 to 15.
But the petitioner had not produced any documents to prove his actual income and part time job.
It is admitted that the petitioner had completed his BBA and hence it deems that there was no difficulty in continuing his studies.

Hence,
in the absence of such documents, I (SCCH3) 11 M.V.C.No.461/2022 just feel it proper to consider the notional income.
As on the date of accident the notional income can be fixed at Rs.15,000/.
The PW.1 had stated that he was aged about 20 years at the time of accident.
In this regard he has got marked his Aadhaar card and Driving licence at Ex.P.9 and 10 which shows that he was born in the year 2001.
So as per these documents the petitioner was aged 21 years at the time of accident.
Thereby proper multiplier comes to "18".
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for loss of future income as Rs.15,000 x 12 x 18 x 12/100 = Rs.3,88,800/ under this head.
b). Pain and sufferings during treatment period:
The petitioner was got admitted in hospital as inpatient from 23.11.2021 to 26.11.2021.
Even there are no other documents on behalf of the petitioner.
But, the discharge summary marked as per Ex.P.8, I just feel it proper to award Rs.25,000/ under this head.
c). Towards medical expenses:
The petitioner has got marked entire medical bills as per Ex.P.12 which amounts to Rs.1,05,452/.
There is no serious dispute with regard to medical bills produced and (SCCH3) 12 M.V.C.No.461/2022 marked by the petitioner.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,05,452/ under this head.

d). Loss of income during laid up period:-
Admittedly the petitioner as per available records could not do any work for 15 days after the accident.
Hence, he is entitled for Rs.7,000/ under this head.

e). Loss of amenities and nutrition food:-
The petitioner had not produced any documents to show that he had incurred amount towards amenities and nutritious food.
But looking into the period of treatment and the nature of injuries, I just feel it proper to award a sum of Rs.10,000/ under this head.

Sri.H.P.Revanth vs Sri.Siddesh.D.R on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70548591/
5 f).
Towards attendent charges and conveyance: The petitioner had took treatment as in patient for nearly 04 days.
It is true that no such documents was produced.
In absence of documents, I just feel it proper to award a sum of Rs.4,000/ under this head.
g). Towards medical expenses : The PW.2 has stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants at the cost of Rs.20,000/.
But in this regard no documents were produced by the petitioner.
Hence under these (SCCH3) 13 M.V.C.No.461/2022 circumstances I just feel it proper to award a sum of Rs.15,000/ under this head.

20. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,55,252/ (Five lakhs fifty five thousand two hundred and fifty two only).
21.
Regarding liability
: As stated above the petitioner has proved the he had sustained injuries due to rash and negligent driving of Car driver.
The respondent No.2 has admitted issuance of policy to the offending Car and its validity.
The said vehicle is owned by the respondent No.1 and duly insured with the respondent No.2.
Hence both respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, issue No.2 is answered partly in affirmative.
22. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2 as above and with regard to awarding the interest is concerned, the petitioner is entitled for simple interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till deposit.
As such I proceed to pass the following: (SCCH3) 14 M.V.C.No.461/2022 ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec. 166 of the M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part, with costs.

The petitioner is entitled for Rs.5,55,252/ (Five lakhs fifty five thousand two hundred and fifty two only) as compensation with interest at 6% p.a (the interest awarded is not applicable to future medical expenses of Rs.15,000/) from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However in view of holding valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 shall deposit the same within time stipulated under section 168(3) of M.V. Act.
On deposit of the compensation amount along with interest accrued, entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through Epayment on proper identification without any further proceedings.

The advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
(SCCH3) 15 M.V.C.No.461/2022 Draw award accordingly.
